headline: Bond investors are starting to treat Oracle and Paramount as one bet on Larry Ellison, whose fortune depends on an AI stock.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: well-sourced analysis of a new credit-market worry, but no new event beyond this week's Paramount financing.
importance_line: Lenders to two of America's largest corporate borrowers now depend on one billionaire whose wealth has fallen by almost 200 billion dollars with Oracle shares, so a slide in Oracle could weaken the safety net under Paramount; the link is investors' reading, not a formal guarantee of Oracle for Paramount.
summary: Bloomberg reports that after Paramount Skydance raised about 52 billion dollars of new debt this week for its Warner Bros. Discovery purchase, and Oracle nearly doubled its long-term debt to more than 160 billion dollars to build AI computing, investors are weighing both against the same backer, Larry Ellison, whose family trust stands behind the Paramount deal. His fortune has dropped by almost 200 billion dollars from its peak as Oracle shares fell more than half, and S&P has cut both companies' ratings; "you have to consider your total Larry Ellison risk," one investor told Bloomberg, while Oracle and Paramount did not comment.
